Strengthen the institutional and technical capacity in Armenia to meet Enhanced Transparency Framework reporting requirements under Paris Agreement in line with national priorities.

The CBIT 2 project in Armenia shall deliver significant socio-economic and environmental benefits by strengthening the country’s climate transparency framework, institutional capacity and policy effectiveness. Institutional sustainability, technical capacity building, and legal reforms shall create a resilient framework for climate action, positioning Armenia as a leader in climate transparency in the region. These efforts shall enhance the country’s ability to respond to climate challenges while unlocking new opportunities for sustainable economic development, social equity, and environmental resilience. Strengthening institutional and legal arrangements for climate transparency shall be a major outcome of CBIT 2. Clearly defined roles and responsibilities, particularly for the Inter-Agency Council on Climate Change and the Statistical Committee, shall institutionalize climate reporting processes and ensure long-term sustainability. The inclusion of the Ministry of Interior in loss and damage data collection shall enhance disaster response coordination, increasing Armenia’s resilience to climate-related disasters. The anticipated adoption of Armenia’s Climate Law in 2025 shall be a cornerstone of the legal framework for climate action, mainstreaming climate considerations across all sectors. Its secondary regulatory framework, supported by this project, will further strengthen implementation. Improved regulatory clarity shall create an environment that attracts climate investments and fosters green economic growth. Advancing technical capacity through tailored Training and Mentorship Programme shall be another key pillar of CBIT2. Equipping government institutions, private sector actors, and civil society organizations with advanced skills in climate data analysis shall improve climate reporting. The inclusion of gender-sensitive training programs shall promote equitable participation, allowing women and marginalized groups to contribute meaningfully to climate governance. Expanding the mentorship component beyond the GHG inventory to include mitigation and adaptation efforts shall help retain institutional knowledge despite staff turnover, ensuring long-term expertise in climate transparency. The socio-economic benefits of these capacity-building efforts shall be substantial. A more skilled workforce in climate-related fields shall foster new employment opportunities, particularly in data analytics, environmental policy, and sustainable finance. Training on sectors-specific issues shall enhance the ability to track climate-related impacts (such as heat-related illnesses), leading to better public health outcomes. Adding a knowledge section to the existing public climate portal shall foster continuous learning and engagement, empowering local communities, businesses, and policymakers to take informed climate action. International knowledge exchange shall be a crucial aspect of the project, with study tours organized for Armenian officials to learn from peer countries with advanced climate transparency systems. Exposure to best practices in climate budgeting, adaptation, and loss and damage reporting shall strengthen Armenia’s implementation capacity. The introduction of innovative data collection and reporting tools, along with digital tool upgrades, shall further streamline climate governance and improve the efficiency of Armenia’s climate policies. Climate mitigation and adaptation are essential for Armenia's long-term economic resilience, energy security, and environmental sustainability. Strategic investments in these areas shall foster green growth, increase energy independence, and drive innovation across sectors, ensuring a cleaner, more productive, and sustainable future. Moreover, strengthening transparency in climate-related data and governance shall support effective decision-making, helping Armenia transition toward a low-carbon economy while ensuring that adaptation measures protect communities and ecosystems from the adverse impacts of climate change.
